title: MAP Sensor Circuit Malfunction
problem: The Engine Control Unit (ECU) detects an implausible signal from the Manifold Absolute Pressure sensor, indicating a potential issue with pressure readings.
symptoms: Engine hesitation; Poor fuel economy; Check Engine Light (CEL) on
actions: Check MAP sensor wiring; Clean MAP sensor port; Replace MAP sensor if faulty

title: MAP Sensor Circuit High Input
problem: The ECU detects a higher than expected voltage signal from the Manifold Absolute Pressure sensor, suggesting a potential short or sensor fault.
symptoms: Rough idle; Decreased engine power; Possible rich running condition
actions: Inspect MAP sensor wiring for shorts; Verify sensor operation; Replace MAP sensor

title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor Circuit
problem: The ECU detects an electrical fault in the Intake Air Temperature sensor circuit, leading to incorrect air density calculations.
symptoms: Incorrect fuel mixture; Reduced engine performance; CEL on
actions: Check IAT sensor wiring; Clean IAT sensor; Replace IAT sensor

title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor Circuit
problem: The ECU detects an abnormal signal from the Engine Coolant Temperature sensor, leading to incorrect temperature readings for fuel management.
symptoms: Hard starting (cold/hot); Incorrect fan operation; Erratic idle
actions: Inspect sensor wiring for damage; Verify sensor resistance; Replace ECT sensor

title: Throttle Position Sensor Circuit Malfunction
problem: The ECU detects an erroneous signal from the Throttle Position Sensor, impacting precise throttle control and engine performance, especially on ride-by-wire systems.
symptoms: Erratic idle; Poor throttle response; Engine may enter limp mode
actions: Calibrate TPS; Check TPS wiring for continuity; Replace throttle body assembly if TPS is integrated

title: Throttle Position Sensor Circuit Low Input
problem: The ECU detects a lower than expected voltage signal from the Throttle Position Sensor, indicating a potential short, open circuit, or sensor failure.
symptoms: Engine idle issues; Reduced acceleration; Limp mode activation
actions: Check TPS wiring for open circuits; Test sensor output voltage; Replace TPS

title: O2 Sensor Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
problem: The ECU identifies an inconsistent or out-of-range signal from the upstream oxygen sensor, affecting air-fuel ratio adjustments.
symptoms: Increased fuel consumption; Rough idle; Emissions failure; CEL on
actions: Check O2 sensor wiring; Inspect sensor for contamination; Replace O2 sensor

title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
problem: The ECU detects an electrical fault in the heater circuit for the upstream oxygen sensor, preventing it from reaching optimal operating temperature.
symptoms: Slow O2 sensor response; Increased emissions; Reduced fuel economy; CEL on
actions: Check O2 sensor heater fuse; Test heater element resistance; Replace O2 sensor

title: O2 Sensor Circuit Malfunction (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
problem: (For V-twin models with two O2 sensors) The ECU identifies an inconsistent or out-of-range signal from the upstream oxygen sensor for the rear cylinder, affecting air-fuel ratio adjustments.
symptoms: Increased fuel consumption; Rough idle; Emissions failure; CEL on
actions: Check O2 sensor wiring; Inspect sensor for contamination; Replace O2 sensor

title: System Too Lean (Bank 1)
problem: The ECU detects that the engine is running with too much air or not enough fuel, indicating a lean condition in the combustion mixture.
symptoms: Engine misfire; Lack of power; Whistling or hissing sounds from intake
actions: Check for vacuum leaks; Inspect fuel pressure and injectors; Examine air filter for restriction

title: System Too Rich (Bank 1)
problem: The ECU detects that the engine is running with too much fuel or not enough air, indicating a rich condition in the combustion mixture.
symptoms: Black smoke from exhaust; Strong fuel smell; Decreased fuel economy; Fouled spark plugs
actions: Check fuel injector leakage; Inspect fuel pressure regulator; Verify O2 sensor function

title: Injector Circuit/Open - Cylinder 1
problem: The ECU detects an electrical fault (open circuit) in the fuel injector for cylinder 1, preventing proper fuel delivery to that cylinder.
symptoms: Engine misfire; Rough idle; Loss of power; Engine runs on one cylinder
actions: Check injector connector and wiring; Test injector resistance; Replace faulty injector

title: Injector Circuit/Open - Cylinder 2
problem: The ECU detects an electrical fault (open circuit) in the fuel injector for cylinder 2, preventing proper fuel delivery to that cylinder.
symptoms: Engine misfire; Rough idle; Loss of power; Engine runs on one cylinder
actions: Check injector connector and wiring; Test injector resistance; Replace faulty injector

title: Fuel Pump Primary Circuit Malfunction
problem: The ECU detects an electrical fault in the primary circuit that controls the fuel pump, potentially preventing the fuel pump from operating.
symptoms: Engine cranks but won't start; No fuel pump prime sound; Intermittent engine cut-out
actions: Check fuel pump relay; Inspect wiring to fuel pump; Verify power supply to pump

title: Random/Multiple Cylinder Misfire Detected
affectedPart: Ignition System; Fuel System; Engine Mechanical
problem: The ECU detects misfires occurring in multiple or random cylinders, indicating a general issue with combustion.
symptoms: Rough engine running; Reduced power; Increased emissions; Vibration
actions: Check spark plugs and ignition coils; Test fuel pressure and injectors; Perform compression test

title: Cylinder 1 Misfire Detected
problem: The ECU detects a misfire specifically in cylinder 1, indicating a localized issue with spark, fuel, or compression.
symptoms: Engine running rough; Loss of power; CEL flashing; Strong fuel smell
actions: Inspect spark plug and coil for cylinder 1; Test injector 1; Perform compression test on cylinder 1

title: Cylinder 2 Misfire Detected
problem: The ECU detects a misfire specifically in cylinder 2, indicating a localized issue with spark, fuel, or compression.
symptoms: Engine running rough; Loss of power; CEL flashing; Strong fuel smell
actions: Inspect spark plug and coil for cylinder 2; Test injector 2; Perform compression test on cylinder 2

title: Crankshaft Position Sensor Circuit Malfunction
problem: The ECU receives an erratic or no signal from the Crankshaft Position Sensor, which is vital for engine timing and RPM calculation.
symptoms: Engine won't start; Intermittent stalling; Tachometer erratic or dead; No spark
actions: Check CKP sensor wiring; Inspect sensor for damage; Replace CKP sensor

title: Camshaft Position Sensor Circuit Malfunction
problem: The ECU receives an erratic or no signal from the Camshaft Position Sensor, affecting valve timing and ignition/fuel synchronization.
symptoms: Engine difficult to start; Reduced engine power; Engine may stall
actions: Check CMP sensor wiring; Inspect sensor for debris; Replace CMP sensor

title: Ignition Coil A Primary/Secondary Circuit Malfunction
problem: The ECU detects an electrical fault in the primary or secondary circuit of the ignition coil for cylinder 1, preventing proper spark delivery.
symptoms: Engine misfire; Rough idle; Loss of power; Strong fuel smell
actions: Check coil wiring and connector; Test coil resistance; Replace ignition coil

title: Ignition Coil B Primary/Secondary Circuit Malfunction
problem: The ECU detects an electrical fault in the primary or secondary circuit of the ignition coil for cylinder 2, preventing proper spark delivery.
symptoms: Engine misfire; Rough idle; Loss of power; Strong fuel smell
actions: Check coil wiring and connector; Test coil resistance; Replace ignition coil

title: EVAP Purge Control Valve Circuit
problem: The ECU detects an electrical fault in the circuit controlling the Evaporative Emission (EVAP) system's purge valve.
symptoms: Check Engine Light (CEL) on; Poor fuel economy; Emission test failure
actions: Inspect purge valve wiring; Test purge valve solenoid; Replace purge valve
location: Near fuel tank or intake manifold

title: Fuel Level Sensor Circuit Malfunction
problem: The ECU detects an electrical fault or out-of-range signal from the fuel level sensor.
symptoms: Inaccurate fuel gauge reading; Fuel warning light on/off randomly
actions: Check sensor wiring; Inspect float mechanism; Replace fuel level sender unit

title: Vehicle Speed Sensor Malfunction
problem: The ECU receives an incorrect or no signal from the Vehicle Speed Sensor, affecting speedometer readings and various engine control strategies.
symptoms: Inaccurate speedometer; ABS/Traction Control issues; Gear selection issues; Engine in limp mode
actions: Check VSS wiring; Clean VSS sensor head; Replace VSS sensor
location: Transmission output shaft or wheel hub

title: Idle Control System Malfunction
affectedPart: Idle Air Control (IAC) Valve / Throttle Body
problem: The ECU detects an issue with the system controlling the engine's idle speed, resulting in unstable idle.
symptoms: High or low idle speed; Stalling at idle; Erratic idle RPM
actions: Clean IAC valve or throttle body; Check vacuum leaks; Calibrate idle system

title: System Voltage Malfunction
problem: The ECU detects that the main system voltage is outside the normal operating range (either too high or too low), which can damage components.
symptoms: Dim lights; Battery not charging; Electronics malfunction; Hard starting
actions: Check battery voltage and connections; Test charging system (stator, regulator); Inspect main fuses

title: System Voltage Low
problem: The ECU detects that the system voltage is consistently below the normal operating threshold, indicating a charging or battery issue.
symptoms: Engine difficult to start; Dim headlights; Electronic systems malfunction
actions: Check battery charge and condition; Test voltage regulator output; Inspect alternator/stator

title: System Voltage High
problem: The ECU detects that the system voltage is consistently above the normal operating threshold, which can damage electrical components.
symptoms: Bulbs blowing frequently; Electronic component failure; Battery overheating
actions: Test voltage regulator output; Inspect regulator/rectifier wiring; Replace regulator/rectifier
location: Typically under the seat or side fairing

title: Serial Communication Link Malfunction
problem: The ECU detects a fault in the communication network (CAN bus) with other control modules, preventing data exchange.
symptoms: Multiple warning lights; Intermittent system failures; Non-functional dashboard components
actions: Inspect CAN bus wiring; Check connectors for corrosion; Diagnose individual modules

title: Internal Control Module Memory Check Sum Error
problem: The ECU has detected an internal error with its memory checksum, indicating a potential corruption of its internal software or data.
symptoms: Engine fails to start; Engine stalls; Incorrect engine operation; Multiple DTCs present
actions: Attempt ECU reflash; Check ECU power and ground; Replace ECU

title: Internal Control Module ROM/RAM Error
problem: The ECU has detected a read-only memory (ROM) or random-access memory (RAM) error, indicating an internal hardware or software malfunction.
symptoms: Engine fails to start; Engine stalls; No communication with diagnostic tools; Unpredictable engine behavior
actions: Attempt ECU reflash; Verify ECU power supply; Replace ECU

title: ECM/PCM Processor Fault
problem: The ECU's internal processor has detected an unrecoverable error, indicating a critical internal hardware or software failure.
symptoms: Engine fails to start; Engine stalls unpredictably; Multiple system failures; No communication with diagnostic tools
actions: Attempt ECU software reflash; Check ECU power and ground; Replace ECU

title: Starter Relay Circuit
problem: The ECU detects an electrical fault in the starter relay circuit, which can prevent the starter motor from engaging.
symptoms: Engine won't crank; No click from starter relay; Intermittent starting issue
actions: Check starter relay fuse; Test starter relay for proper function; Inspect wiring to starter relay

title: Fuel Pump Control Circuit/Open
problem: The ECU detects an open circuit or electrical fault in the control circuit for the fuel pump, preventing it from operating.
symptoms: Engine cranks but won't start; No fuel pressure; Fuel pump does not prime
actions: Check fuel pump control wiring; Test fuel pump driver module; Replace faulty relay/module
location: Under fuel tank or near ECU

title: Sensor Reference Voltage 'A' Circuit/Open
problem: The ECU detects an open circuit or low voltage on the 5-volt reference circuit 'A', which supplies power to multiple sensors.
symptoms: Multiple sensor-related DTCs; Engine stalls; No throttle response
actions: Check wiring for shorts to ground/open circuits; Inspect connected sensors for internal shorts; Isolate faulty sensor

title: Sensor Reference Voltage 'B' Circuit/Open
problem: The ECU detects an open circuit or low voltage on the 5-volt reference circuit 'B', which supplies power to other groups of sensors.
symptoms: Multiple sensor-related DTCs; Engine stalls; ABS/TC system errors
actions: Check wiring for shorts to ground/open circuits; Inspect connected sensors for internal shorts; Isolate faulty sensor

title: (Ducati Specific) Throttle Body Position Sensor Correlation Error
problem: The ECU detects a discrepancy between the readings of the primary and secondary throttle position sensors within the ride-by-wire throttle body.
symptoms: Engine in limp mode; Erratic throttle response; Traction control errors
actions: Check throttle body wiring; Perform throttle body calibration; Replace throttle body assembly

title: (Ducati Specific) ECU Internal Supervision Error
problem: The ECU's internal monitoring system has detected an error in its self-diagnostic processes or critical internal parameters.
symptoms: Engine fails to start; Intermittent power loss; Unpredictable engine behavior
actions: Attempt ECU software reflash; Verify ECU power and ground; Replace ECU

title: ABS Wheel Speed Sensor Front Circuit
problem: The ABS control unit detects an electrical malfunction or inconsistent signal from the front wheel speed sensor, affecting ABS operation.
symptoms: ABS warning light on; ABS system disabled; Inconsistent brake feel (if sensor intermittently fails)
actions: Check sensor wiring; Clean sensor head and reluctor ring; Replace front wheel speed sensor

title: ABS Wheel Speed Sensor Rear Circuit
problem: The ABS control unit detects an electrical malfunction or inconsistent signal from the rear wheel speed sensor, affecting ABS operation.
symptoms: ABS warning light on; ABS system disabled; Inconsistent brake feel (if sensor intermittently fails)
actions: Check sensor wiring; Clean sensor head and reluctor ring; Replace rear wheel speed sensor

title: Steering Angle Sensor Malfunction
problem: The ABS/Traction Control unit detects an implausible or missing signal from the steering angle sensor, critical for cornering ABS and traction control.
symptoms: ABS/Traction Control warning light on; Cornering ABS/TC disabled; Riding modes malfunction
actions: Check sensor wiring; Calibrate steering angle sensor; Replace steering angle sensor

title: Immobilizer Communication Fault
affectedPart: Immobilizer Control Unit; ECU; Key Transponder
problem: The ECU cannot establish proper communication with the immobilizer system or read the key transponder, preventing engine start.
symptoms: Engine cranks but won't start; Immobilizer light flashing; Key not recognized
actions: Try spare key; Check immobilizer antenna; Diagnose immobilizer module/ECU for programming

title: Instrument Panel Communication Fault
problem: The ECU or other control units detect a loss of communication with the instrument panel, preventing display of vital information.
symptoms: Dashboard lights off/flashing; No speedometer/tachometer reading; Warning lights absent
actions: Check dash power and ground; Inspect CAN bus wiring to dash; Replace instrument panel if faulty

title: ABS Control Unit Communication Fault
problem: The main ECU or other modules detect a loss of communication with the ABS control unit, disabling the ABS system.
symptoms: ABS warning light on; Brakes operate without ABS; Multiple system errors
actions: Check ABS unit power/ground; Inspect CAN bus wiring to ABS unit; Diagnose/Replace ABS control unit

title: Traction Control Unit Communication Fault
problem: The main ECU or other modules detect a loss of communication with the Traction Control Unit, disabling TC functionality.
symptoms: Traction Control warning light on; TC system disabled; Riding modes malfunction
actions: Check TCU power/ground; Inspect CAN bus wiring to TCU; Diagnose/Replace TCU
location: Integrated with ECU or separate module

title: TPS Out of Range / Initial Position Error (Legacy Ducati)
problem: The ECU detects that the throttle position sensor's voltage is outside the expected range during initialization or calibration, indicating an incorrect idle position.
symptoms: Engine won't start or starts with very high idle; Throttle response issues; Limp home mode
actions: Perform TPS reset/calibration; Check TPS wiring; Replace TPS/throttle body.

title: O2 Sensor Open Circuit / Heater Fault (Legacy Ducati)
problem: The ECU detects an open circuit in the O2 sensor's signal or heater circuit, preventing accurate exhaust gas measurement.
symptoms: Increased fuel consumption; Poor engine performance; CEL on
actions: Check O2 sensor wiring; Test sensor heater resistance; Replace O2 sensor.

title: Fuel Pump Relay Fault (Legacy Ducati)
problem: The ECU detects an electrical fault with the fuel pump relay, preventing proper operation of the fuel pump.
symptoms: Engine cranks but won't start; No fuel pump prime sound; Fuel pressure loss
actions: Check fuel pump relay and fuse; Inspect wiring to relay; Replace fuel pump relay.

title: Injector 1 Open Circuit (Legacy Ducati)
problem: The ECU detects an open circuit on the fuel injector for cylinder 1, resulting in no fuel delivery to that cylinder.
symptoms: Engine misfire; Rough idle; Loss of power; Engine runs on one cylinder
actions: Check injector 1 wiring and connector; Test injector 1 resistance; Replace injector 1.

title: Injector 2 Open Circuit (Legacy Ducati)
problem: The ECU detects an open circuit on the fuel injector for cylinder 2, resulting in no fuel delivery to that cylinder.
symptoms: Engine misfire; Rough idle; Loss of power; Engine runs on one cylinder.
actions: Check injector 2 wiring and connector; Test injector 2 resistance; Replace injector 2.
